species.name: Leafcutter Ant
mustRead: three-part body with a pinched narrow waist
elbowed antennae
spined thorax carrying a leaf fragment overhead
species.note: the thorax bears distinct backward-pointing spines; the head is oversized with big cutting jaws

species.name: Butterfly
mustRead: two pairs of broad scaled wings
clubbed knob-tipped antennae
coiled watch-spring proboscis
species.note: six legs attach only to the thorax, and the antennae end in clubs, not the feathery plumes of a moth

species.name: Termite
mustRead: pale soft translucent segmented body
straight bead-string antennae
broad joint where the abdomen meets the thorax
species.note: workers are blind and unpigmented; there is no wasp waist and the antennae are straight, unlike an ant's elbowed pair

species.name: Cicada
mustRead: broad transparent veined wings tented roof-like over the body
blunt wide head with eyes pushed to the corners
short stout barrel body
species.note: wings are held tent-like over the back at rest, not spread flat

species.name: Mantis
mustRead: spined raptorial forelegs folded in prayer
triangular head that swivels on a neck
long slender prothorax raising the front of the body
species.note: only a mantis truly has a neck - the head turns independently of the body

species.name: Locust
mustRead: hugely enlarged folded hind jumping legs
long narrow wings folded flat along the back
short antennae and a tall flat-sided head
species.note: antennae are short - long thread antennae belong to katydids and crickets, not locusts

species.name: Dung Beetle
mustRead: glossy armoured domed black body
flat spade-shaped head used as a rake
toothed rake-like digging forelegs
species.note: many species carry a horn on the head or thorax; the wing cases are smooth and hard, not textured

species.name: Orchid Bee
mustRead: brilliant metallic green, blue or gold body
extremely long tongue trailing back beneath the body
swollen polished hind tibia on males
species.note: shiny and jewel-like rather than fuzzy - it should not read as a striped honeybee

species.name: Bee
mustRead: furry thorax with banded amber-and-black abdomen
two pairs of clear veined wings
pollen basket on the hind leg
species.note: Read as a honeybee. Four wings, not two; the body is fuzzy, not smooth like a wasp's.

species.name: Mosquito
mustRead: long needle proboscis jutting straight forward
six very long dangling legs
narrow scale-fringed wings
species.note: Body hangs at an angle with the hind legs kicked up; only two wings, not four.

species.name: Black Fly
mustRead: strongly humped thorax over a bowed head
short broad clear wings
stubby compact dark body

species.name: Dragonfly
mustRead: two pairs of long transparent net-veined wings held out flat
huge globe compound eyes filling the head
long slender rod abdomen
species.note: Wings stay spread at rest, never folded back over the body like a damselfly's.

species.name: Grasshopper
mustRead: huge angled jumping hind legs rising above the back
long tapered abdomen
short stout antennae and slanted face

species.name: Cricket
mustRead: antennae longer than the whole body
flat wings laid over a rounded back
cranked jumping hind legs

species.name: Ant
mustRead: three distinct body lumps pinched by a narrow waist
elbowed antennae
six thin legs splayed from the middle segment
species.note: Generic name read as a representative worker ant. The waist petiole between thorax and abdomen is the read; drawing it as a smooth two-part body makes it a beetle.

species.name: Honeybee
mustRead: furry thorax with a banded amber-and-black abdomen
two pairs of clear veined wings
pollen baskets on the hind legs

species.name: Bumblebee
mustRead: fat rounded fully furry body
broad bands of black and yellow fuzz
wings small relative to the bulky body

species.name: Ladybug
mustRead: strongly domed hemispherical shell
spotted red wing cases split down the middle
tiny black head tucked under a shield
species.note: Almost always drawn from above; in true side profile it is a low dome and the spots barely read, so the silhouette must carry the arc of the shell.

species.name: Water Beetle
mustRead: smooth oval domed wing cases
flattened hair-fringed hind legs used as oars
short clubbed antennae on a tucked head

species.name: Caddisfly
mustRead: hairy wings folded tent-like over the back
very long thread-thin antennae held forward
moth-like drab body
species.note: Commonly drawn as the larva in its pebble case; the adult is a moth-like insect with roof-folded wings and no coiled proboscis.

species.name: Mayfly
mustRead: two or three long hair-thin tail filaments
triangular wings held upright together over the back
slender upcurved abdomen

species.name: Stonefly
mustRead: wings folded flat and overlapping down the back
two short stout tail cerci
long antennae on a flat squarish head

species.name: Damselfly
mustRead: needle-thin stick abdomen
wings held closed together over the back at rest
hammerhead face with widely separated eyes
species.note: Not a dragonfly - the eyes are set apart on the sides and the wings fold rather than staying spread.

species.name: Water Strider
mustRead: extremely long splayed middle and hind legs
dimples denting the water surface under the feet
narrow slim boat-shaped body
